cycles.method: MKII OS 1.40C, package 0c5632f6, RAM base fac1523234f4bb0b. The longest guarded callback in the T1 24-bit stereo USB audio and MIDI comparison was 18,310 ticks of the 132 MHz timer. This includes stock Flex and interruptions. The earlier sequencer and MIDI-only comparison peaked at 17,845 ticks. The static Grain-only zero-wait-state model gives 192,656 cycles for 16 and 359,568 for 32 source frames. External memory, stock callees and interrupt interference remain unbounded.

load.method: Same 12-second USB MIDI trace on the 100 BPM card-free Part, stereo R3 on T1 and T5. Empty-inventory Flex peaked at 70.3% of a frame. One six-voice Grain on T1 or T5 peaked at 89.6% or 93.0% respectively. All three windows showed a median 100% CPU meter and zero new skipped renders. Opening 20-channel USB audio separately produced skips on both Grain tracks. See evidence/timing/recorder.json.

stress.droppedExplanation: One trace submitted 13,249 USB MIDI events in 12 seconds. Receive errors, transmit drops and render skips held steady in the MIDI-only windows, including a completed Part 2/1 change. End-to-end message delivery and stuck notes were not counted. The 20-channel audio capture had render drops, counted separately in evidence/timing/recorder.json. On the 0.7.11 development twin, adding USB audio to the MIDI workload produced 658 skipped renders on the six-voice T1. A separate two-voice trial stalled at the panel after a 60-second combined flood. See evidence/timing/combined-load.json.
